messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT — automated paging: region=eu-1, symptom=error-rate-high on /v1/generate, automatic traffic-shift initiated to eu-2. Pager: PAGER-3342.

ajay (oncall): acked. I'm on it. seeing elevated 5xxs and latency spikes for EU customers.

maria (SRE): I'm pulling traffic logs from the console and routing table. DNS lookups for eu-1 are failing intermittently — NXDOMAIN spikes around the same time as the error rate.

sam (eng): any infra deploys in eu-1 in the last hour?

ajay (oncall): no deploys. autoscaler events only. root cause unknown.

lia (support): a customer (acme-inc) just filed a ticket: "requests returning 502/504, embeddings time out" — they're in Amsterdam.

maria (SRE): running quick health check:
```bash
curl -sS -I https://api.eu-1.redwood.ai/health || true
```
returned:
```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Server: nginx
```
So upstreams are returning 503s.

sam (eng): I see traceroute from a worker into eu-1 hitting intermittent packet loss at the cloud-provider's router. Could be an AZ-level network flapping.

ajay (oncall): ok. auto-traffic-shift kicked but looks like some flows still trying to route to eu-1 and timing out -> causing errors. We need to ensure all edge routers stop sending new sessions to eu-1.

maria (SRE): I'm applying a temporary routing policy override to prefer eu-2 and reduce weight for eu-1 to 0. Command (console):
```
rwctl routing update --region eu-1 --weight 0 --region eu-2 --weight 100 --reason "emergency: eu-1 network instability"
```
applied, waiting for propagation.

ops-bot: routing update accepted, request id=req-78b2. Edge config push started.

ajay (oncall): changing DNS TTL to 30s for api.redwood.ai in EU zone to accelerate failover.

maria (SRE): also initiating drain for eu-1 instances to avoid split-brain. Runbook step: drain -> stop accepting new sessions -> allow KV cache to warm in eu-2.

sam (eng): posting the snippet to verify active region from a client perspective:
```bash
curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/identify-region | jq .region
# should return eu-2 after propagation
```

lia (support): drafting a short status update for customers — impact: increased 5xx and latency for EU region; mitigation: traffic moved to eu-2; ETA for resolution: 30-45m while we validate. @kelly want to sign off? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

kelly (product): yes go ahead. add note we are monitoring telemetry and will update every 15m.

ajay (oncall): handing off to maria for the next 30m while I follow up with the cloud provider on the AZ-level network update. If anything changes ping me @ajay.

maria (SRE): taking over. current checks: error-rate dropped from 5.2% -> 0.8% after routing update, but a handful of sticky sessions still timing out. Working on purging stale routes on the edge.

ops-bot: edge push completed, all edges now prefer eu-2.

maria (SRE): verified client-region check: returned eu-2 for 95% of probes. Running additional probes across POPs.

lia (support): ticket queue: 8 new EU tickets flagged as high-priority, triaging and sending update to affected customers.

sam (eng): noticed redis KV latency spike during failover — might be due to cross-region reads. Suggest setting failover-read-preference local-only for now.

maria (SRE): applied KV read preference change in the routing profile. Monitor shows 99th latency dropping.

ajay (oncall): cloud provider says they have a partial outage in AZ eu-1a; they're moving traffic. They also confirmed DNS edge caching might still have stale entries in some ISPs.

kelly (product): preparing a status page message to explain root cause as "AZ networking instability causing partial regional degradation; automated traffic shift to backup region mitigated most customer impact; follow-up postmortem forthcoming."

ops-bot: metric alert cleared: error-rate at 0.3% for eu region.

maria (SRE): closing this thread for active mitigation. We'll open a postmortem ticket: PM-445. Action items: 1) confirm complete recovery for all customers, 2) postmortem, 3) add extra edge checks to detect stale DNS caching earlier.

ajay (oncall): reassigning paging attribution to incident-owner=maria. I'll remain on-standby for cloud provider updates. Good job team. :thumbsup:
